panel.route.emptyText.en: Its dashboard was deleted, and there are no other dashboards on its Homey.
panel.route.emptyText.context: Text under the title "This wall panel has nothing to show". A Homey is the smart-home hub the dashboards belong to.

panel.route.emptyTitle.en: This wall panel has nothing to show
panel.route.emptyTitle.context: Title of the message on a wall panel page when the dashboard of the panel was deleted and the Homey has no other dashboard to show instead.

panel.route.failedText.en: Check your connection and try again.
panel.route.failedText.context: Text under the title "Couldn’t open the wall panel". Two buttons follow: try again, and leave the wall panel.

panel.route.failedTitle.context: Title of the message on a wall panel page (a dashboard shown full screen on a tablet or kiosk) when loading the panel failed, for example because the connection broke.

panel.route.leave.context: Button on the wall panel page when the panel cannot open. It stops using this browser as a wall panel and goes back to the Tiledash app. A command.

panel.route.unnamed.context: Stands in for the name of a wall panel that was opened from an old dashboard link and so has no name of its own. Shown in the options bar of the wall panel screen.

panel.screen.bar.context: Name of the small options bar that appears at the top of a wall panel screen, read out by screen readers. Not visible as text.

panel.screen.barName.context: Text at the left of the options bar on a wall panel screen: the name of the wall panel and the name of the dashboard it shows now, separated by a dot.

params.dashboard: The dashboard’s name. Chosen by the owner; not translated.
params.panel: The wall panel’s name, such as "Hallway". Chosen by the owner; not translated.

panel.screen.edit.context: Button in the options bar of a wall panel screen. It opens the dashboard for editing in the app.

panel.screen.fullScreen.context: Name and tooltip of the small button at the bottom of a wall panel screen that makes the browser show the page full screen.

panel.screen.hide.context: Name of the small × button of the options bar on a wall panel screen, read out by screen readers. It hides the bar again. Not visible as text.

panel.screen.holdForOptions.context: Name of the invisible button in the top-left corner of a wall panel screen, read out by screen readers. Holding it brings up the options bar. Not visible as text.

panel.screen.leaveFullScreen.context: Name and tooltip of the small button at the bottom of a wall panel screen that makes the browser go back from full screen to a window.

panel.screen.leavePanel.context: Name and tooltip of the small button at the bottom of a wall panel screen, and the label of a button in the options bar. It stops showing the wall panel and goes back to the Tiledash app. A command.

panel.screen.statusLive.context: Name of the quiet status dot in the corner of a wall panel screen when everything works and values are up to date, read out by screen readers. On e-ink screens it is not shown as text.

panel.screen.statusOffline.context: Small status word in the corner of a wall panel screen: the connection to Tiledash is lost and the values on screen may be old. Also the name of that status for screen readers.

panel.screen.statusReconnecting.context: Small status word in the corner of a wall panel screen: the connection was lost and is being restored. Also the name of that status for screen readers.

panel.screen.unnamedPanel.context: Stands in for the name of a wall panel that has no name of its own, in the options bar at the top of a wall panel screen, before the dashboard’s name.

panel.screen.unpair.context: Button in the options bar of a paired wall panel screen (a tablet that was paired with a code). It asks whether to cut the link between this screen and the account.

panel.screen.updated.context: Small status text in the corner of a wall panel on an e-ink screen, which cannot show a pulsing dot: the clock time the values on screen were taken.

params.time: The clock time, such as 21:43. Already formatted.

panel.screen.wake.context: Name of the invisible button that covers a sleeping wall panel screen, read out by screen readers. A touch on it wakes the screen. Not visible as text.
